constraints: Use human gene sets — the data is Homo sapiens kidney; do not use the mouse or rat collections that are also present in the store

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with latent-factor correction
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample Salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv) with a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) giving condition only: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, human kidney. The profiling caveat is the whole analytical problem: PCA splits the samples into two clusters of six that do NOT track condition, and no batch column was recorded. That is an unmeasured source of variation with the same cardinality as the design, so it can be (a) orthogonal to condition — 3 treated + 3 control per cluster, in which case it is nuisance variation that can be modelled and removed, gaining power; (b) partially aligned; or (c) perfectly confounded with condition, in which case NO method can separate treatment from the hidden factor and the honest answer is that the effect is unidentifiable. The plan therefore refuses to run a naive contrast first and instead makes identifiability the gating question.

T1S1 reconstructs the latent structure explicitly: import counts, verify they are integers (the record does not say whether a length correction was applied by tximport, so this must be checked and reported, not assumed), filter low-count genes, VST-transform, recompute PCA, and cross-tabulate an unsupervised 2-group partition (hierarchical clustering on sample correlation + k=2 k-means on the top PCs) against condition. It reports the cross-tab and a condition-vs-cluster association test, which classifies the design into the orthogonal / partial / confounded case above. It also checks whether the split is explained by an observable technical proxy that is recoverable from the data itself — library size, detection rate, GC-free proxies such as the fraction of counts in the top genes — since a 'hidden batch' that is really a depth artefact is fixable by normalization alone.

T1S2 runs the primary DE. DESeq2 on raw counts with ~ condition, and in parallel a latent-factor-adjusted model. Because no batch was recorded, the adjustment must be estimated from the data: svaseq (sva is installed) on the normalized counts with the full model ~condition and null model ~1, with the number of surrogate variables chosen by the package estimator but capped, then ~ SV1 (+ SV2) + condition. If T1S1 found the split orthogonal to condition, this is the model to trust and it should recover more DE genes at higher precision. If the split is confounded, sva will absorb the treatment effect and the step must report that rather than present the shrunken result as the answer. A third, deliberately blunt comparison — inserting the empirical cluster label as a covariate — is run only when the cross-tab shows it is estimable, to show how much of the naive gene list is cluster-driven. Deliverable: one results table per model with concordance statistics between them, and an explicit statement of which model is the primary result and why.

T1S3 is the sensitivity/diagnostic layer: p-value histograms per model (a hidden factor produces a characteristic non-uniform null), independent-filtering and dispersion plots, the number of genes changing sign or losing significance between models, and a leave-one-sample-out stability check on the top genes given n=6 per arm. It exists because with 12 samples and an unexplained axis of variation, the credibility of the gene list rests on these diagnostics, not on the FDR number.

T2S1 takes the primary ranked gene list into enrichment against the staged human MSigDB hallmark and GO-BP collections (confirmed present under /mnt/refs, HGNC symbols) plus human WikiPathways, using fgsea on the full shrunken-LFC ranking rather than a threshold-based ORA, because the effect may be modest once the latent factor is modelled. It must run on the primary model's ranking and, as a contrast, on the naive ranking, and report which enriched terms survive latent-factor adjustment — terms present only in the naive ranking are candidates for hidden-factor artefacts. Kidney-tissue interpretation is expected but the step must not assert mechanism beyond what the statistics support.

Package availability was checked: sva 3.60.0, DESeq2 1.52.0, limma, edgeR, apeglm, ashr, fgsea, clusterProfiler, EnhancedVolcano, pheatmap are all installed; RUVSeq is NOT installed, so RUV-based correction is deliberately not planned (ruv 0.9.7.1 exists but takes a different, non-count interface and is only a fallback). Reference gene sets are confirmed staged for human.

Human hallmark, GO-BP and WikiPathways GMTs are staged in this environment; the human UniProt ID-mapping table is staged for identifier conversion if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Reports the gene identifier type found in counts.csv and, if mapping was needed, the mapping rate and genes lost
fgsea results tables written for the primary and the naive rankings against each available collection, with NES, p, and BH FDR
Side-by-side term table classifying significant terms as shared / adjusted-only / naive-only
Leading-edge gene lists for the top 10 terms of the adjusted ranking
Names any requested collection that was absent from the reference store rather than silently substituting another
constraints: Use human gene sets — the data is Homo sapiens kidney; do not use the mouse or rat collections that are also present in the store
Rank on the shrunken LFC from the primary model, not on -log10(p) alone
Report BH-adjusted enrichment p-values; do not report nominal enrichment p as significant
Set a fixed random seed so the permutation-based FDR is reproducible
caveats: GO-BP sets are nested, so significant terms arrive in correlated blocks — collapse redundant parent/child terms before reporting a count
An enrichment surviving latent-factor adjustment is more credible but is still derived from 12 samples with no independent validation cohort
If sva absorbed the treatment effect (flagged in T1S2), the adjusted ranking may be near-null and the comparison should be reported as uninformative rather than as an absence of biology
